summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Factor V Leiden deficiency, prior DVT/PE, chronic hemoptysis, ventral hernia, and splenectomy was admitted for acute exacerbation of chronic abdominal pain and worsening hemoptysis. Imaging showed no acute abdominal or pulmonary pathology. His abdominal pain was managed with continuation of oxycodone and initiation of amitriptyline for chronic pain. Hemoptysis and hematuria were attributed to chronic cough and anticoagulation with Lovenox, which may be slightly overdosed given his current weight. Due to syringe limitations, Lovenox dose could not be reduced, and he was discharged on prior dose with hematology follow-up. He remained stable, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and close outpatient follow-up.
